sections.h2: Who to call about Athens County property tax
sections.html:
Two offices matter. The county auditor sets values and takes exemption applications at 15 S. Court Street in Athens, and its Real Estate Division answers at 740-592-3223. The treasurer mails the bills and takes payment. That office also runs delinquent payment plans, escrow plans and mobile home tax.

The treasurer chairs the county land bank, too. A run-down vacant house with back taxes can draw that office's attention as well as a buyer's.

Athens County is hill country, 508 square miles of steep ridges and creek valleys drained mostly by the Hocking River. The city of Athens is the seat and the largest community. The 2020 count was 62,431 people and 26,386 housing units, of which 10.2% were vacant. Among occupied homes, 45.6% were rented.

That renter share means many sellers here own rental houses near campus. If you are one of them, check each parcel's owner-occupancy status with the auditor before you sell.

The county prints the real due dates on your bill, so read the current one rather than relying on last year's calendar. State law, ORC 323.12, sets the baseline at December 31 for the whole bill, or half by then and the rest by June 20. A mailed payment is timely if its U.S. Postal Service postmark falls on or before the last day.

Ohio allows no grace period, so a late payment normally draws a penalty automatically. Mailed checks can run late because the Postal Service no longer postmarks on the day it receives mail. An electronic payment costs $0.50. If paying in full is a stretch, call or stop in at the treasurer's office and ask about a payment plan. Mobile home bills go out right after the regular bills with the same due date.

sections.h2: Why bills vary across the county
sections.html:
The county mixes a university city, an old coal and salt district, and farm and forest land. Each of those uses can fall in a different school district and township, and that changes the levies stacked on a parcel. Five school districts serve residents: Alexander Local, Athens City, Federal Hocking Local, Nelsonville-York City and Trimble Local.

Two houses of similar size, one in Athens and one in Trimble, can carry different bills. Ask the auditor for the taxing district code on your parcel to see why.

Athens County's next countywide reappraisal is tax year 2026. New values apply as of January 1, 2026 and reach bills payable in 2027. The auditor posts values online and asks owners to check acreage, building size and construction details, then call the Real Estate Division about errors. The website shows only the new value, so compare it against your second-half 2025 bill.

The auditor also summarizes several late-2025 state laws that limit automatic tax growth:

  • House Bill 186 creates an Inflation Cap Credit for some school districts hit by the 20-mill floor, itemized on the bill.
  • House Bill 335 limits growth in inside millage during valuation reset years to inflation.
  • House Bill 129 changes how the school district 20-mill floor is calculated, beginning with tax year 2026.

These laws do not eliminate property taxes, repeal voted levies, reduce school bond millage or freeze values.

A complaint goes to the county auditor, who passes it to the Board of Revision. Filing stays open to the end of March of the next tax year, or until first-half collection closes if that is later (ORC 5715.19(A)(1)). The treasurer sits on the Board of Revision.

Parties must get hearing notice ten days ahead, and the board has 180 days from the last filing day to decide. While you wait, you can tender tax on your claimed value, and the treasurer must accept it. If you owe more at the end, interest runs on the shortfall. A second complaint in the same interim period needs something new, such as an arm's-length sale, casualty, a major improvement or a fifteen percent swing in occupancy.

Relief programs available to Athens County homeowners
ProgramWho qualifiesHow to apply
Homestead exemptionOwners aged 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, who live in the home on January 1; new applicants face an income cap of Ohio adjusted gross income below $38,600 for tax year 2024Mail the application to the auditor by December 31
Disabled veteran increaseOwners 100 percent disabled from service; the exemption rose from $26,200 to $52,300Form DTE 105I
Owner occupancy reductionOwners living in the home as a principal residence on January 1, limited to one Ohio home per owner and spouseForm DTE 105C
CAUVFarmland of ten acres or more in exclusive agricultural use, or smaller tracts with at least $2,500 average yearly farm income over three yearsCall 740-592-3223

The income cap shown is for tax year 2024, so ask the auditor for the current limit.

Ask the treasurer for a payoff, and check whether a payment plan balance is open. Under ORC 319.202 the grantee files a value statement with the auditor at transfer. It records what the seller said about homestead or owner-occupancy reductions and about CAUV status, and a farm leaving CAUV can face a recoupment charge.

ORC 319.54(G)(3) prices the auditor's conveyance fee at $1 or 10 cents per $100 of value or fraction, whichever is more. The grantor covers it, along with any Chapter 322 county transfer tax. Ask the Athens County auditor whether such a tax applies.

An inherited house, a house with tenants or a house that needs work can close as-is without changing any of this. A buyer paying cash skips the lender, but the payoff, the value statement and the fee all still happen. Start with the treasurer's payoff so you know what comes out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Athens County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: The due dates are printed on each bill. State law sets the baseline at December 31, or half by then and the rest by June 20. There is no grace period, so late payments are penalized.

faqs.q: Does the Athens County treasurer offer payment plans?
faqs.a: Yes. Call or visit the treasurer's office to ask about one. An electronic payment carries a $0.50 fee.

faqs.q: When does the new Athens County reappraisal show up on my bill?
faqs.a: On bills payable in 2027, using values as of January 1, 2026. Check the auditor's posted value against your second-half 2025 bill.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the Athens County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Homeowners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, who live there on January 1, with an income cap for new applicants. The auditor takes applications until December 31.

faqs.q: When does the window to contest a valuation close?
faqs.a: At the end of March in the next tax year, or at the close of first-half collection if that is later (ORC 5715.19(A)(1)). The auditor receives the complaint and passes it to the Board of Revision.
